newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas says could replace BHP in Vietnam field.
newsitem.headline: Petronas says could replace BHP in Vietnam field.

text.p: Malaysia's state-run oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) said on Monday it is prepared to take over as operator of Vietnam's Dai Hung oil field from Broken Hill Proprietary Company Ltd (BHP).

"We have said that we are prepared to take over the operatorship, but subject to all parties agreeing to it in order to get the consent from the government of Vietnam," Petronas president Mohamed Hassan Marican told reporters.
He was speaking after the opening of a conference on natural gas in the Western Pacific.

The Dai Hung field, once thought to be one of Asia's largest, is owned by a consortium comprising BHP with a 43.75 percent stake, Petronas with 20 percent, Vietnam's state-owned PetroVietnam with 15 percent and Total Sa and Sumitomo Corp with 10.625 percent each.
BHP said in September it would be interested in any reasonable offer for its stake in Dai Hung.

The company, which fully wrote down its A$151 million Dai Hung investment in its 1995/96 accounts, had been trying to renegotiate terms of its contract with PetroVietnam after estimates of the field's reserves were slashed.
Asked whether Petronas has had discussions with BHP about taking over operation of the field, Hassan said: "Only as partners."
BHP is still the operator of the field, he said.
"BHP is leading the discussion with PetroVietnam to resolve some of the issues on the development of the field," he added.
According to initial estimates, Dai Hung had recoverable oil reserves of 700 million barrels. That was later revised downwards to 100 million barrels.
